pooled.note: NOT ONE of the 58 solved items had the solver pick a different option. Every disagreement is the solver naming a SECOND DEFENSIBLE option (13) or saying the passages do not settle it (4). That is a different defect from a wrong key: it points at distractors that are not clearly wrong, which is the same finding that produced the cert_notes rule about every distractor being a mistake someone could actually make.

clauses.note: ZERO items across all four certifications cite a clause address no source holds. The 9 container citations (3 AIMS-IA, 6 ISMS-IA) name a heading whose children are held and whose own row does not exist -- the PROMPT-104 container-citation backlog item, not an item defect.

costs_usd.aims_ia_caveat: AIMS-IA's cause split is derived from its REJECTED runs' classification strings, because PROMPT-142 s5 recorded prose rather than the structured fields and the prose was then stripped for licensed text. For a rejected run those strings are distinct and reliable; it was the ACCEPTED runs' classification that was unreliable, and agreement needs no cause. The other three read the cause from the response's own fields.

library_findings.what: ISO/IEC 27000 3.77 (vulnerability, an 18-word definition) held 282 words: the extractor did not bound it at the next top-level heading, so it swallowed clause 4 and 4.1.
library_findings.impact: Two R2 survivors quoted that clause-4 text as support and both now FAIL verbatim: #10 in its KEY (the director spotted the symptom in the explanation) and #5 in a distractor support (not visible from the report).
library_findings.repaired: SOURCE-PASSAGES.json patched and recorded in PASSAGE-REPAIRS.json; the extractor itself is NOT yet fixed.
library_findings.detector: scripts/check-passage-runon.mjs, 6 controls. 48 passages flagged library-wide: 6 on the strong arm (an embedded later clause heading) and the rest on an annex cross-reference, which is usually legitimate.

model_decisions.decision: The WRITER stays on claude-opus-5. The SOLVER was never in question.
model_decisions.tested: claude-sonnet-5 as the writer, R6 (ISMSF-R6), solver held on claude-opus-5

measured.items_that_never_reached_a_gate: 41 of 89 (15 of 22 writer batches failed on the first call)
measured.writer_share_of_a_round: 39.1% across R3-R5, so a 5x cheaper writer caps the saving at 31.3%

model_decisions.why: The two gates Sonnet failed most ARE the grounding guarantee: verbatim means the quote is not in the passage, modal-fidelity means the item states as required what the standard recommends. The director's own read found the rest -- implausible distractors beside a sensible key. A cheaper writer whose characteristic failure is mis-quoting the source is not cheaper.
kept_from_the_experiment: --writer-model and --solver-model: a model change is a flag, not a code change.
Spend metered PER MODEL, so a mixed run cannot be priced at one rate.
The balanced-bracket truncation test (the old one was defeated by the nested options array).
model_decisions.not_pursued: The empty-response mode (9 of 37 Sonnet writer calls returned no text). Ruled: it only occurred on Sonnet, so it is not chased.
model_decisions.measured_and_notable: The director read the rejects as 'the key is far longer than the rest'. Measured, it is NOT a length effect: key-is-the-longest-option 44% on the 9 rejects against 50% on the 20 accepts, mean key/longest-rival 1.02 against 1.07. The existing length-cue rule correctly did not fire and no length rule would have caught these. The defect is distractor PLAUSIBILITY, which CLAUDE.md s13 already records as needing an SME rather than a gate.

model_decisions.certification_scope: ISMS-IA and the certifications after it
model_decisions.decision: DEFAULT WRITER IS claude-sonnet-5-5. The solver stays claude-opus-5.

evidence.what_settled_it: R2 was a SAME-TASK CROSSOVER and both writers survived 13 of 20 -- identical. R1 25-point gap was the task mix. After the PROMPT-127 s4 distractor-plausibility note the director rejects were 1 to 0, and that one was a cross-writer duplicate rather than a weak item.
evidence.what_is_given_up: Opus scenarios are richer. The director judged Sonnet R2 items exam-grade.

ISMS-F._what: Closed PROMPT-125 s3. ISMS-F is live: 263 grounded items, 896 approved rows per language.

session._caveat: WALL CLOCK between the first and last instrumented stage run, not time at the keyboard. Stages 5 to 9 are not instrumented, so work after the last stage-4 run is outside this window.

spend_usd._NOT_RECOVERABLE: THE TRANSLATION STAGE. The spend happens on the run that makes the calls; the artifact is written by the run that writes the rows, which resumes from the checkpoint and legitimately spends $0. So every ISMSF-TRANSLATION-*.json records usd: 0 and the per-round translation cost is gone. 304 item-translations with no price on any of them. Three runs were observed live and are the only translation figures that exist: PROMPT-123 $0.7531 for 5 items, PROMPT-124 $0.2315 for 1, PROMPT-125 $0.8520 for 5. NOT extrapolated to the other 293: a rate times a count is an estimate, and this file does not carry estimates. FIXED for ISMS-IA: the checkpoint now carries usd_cumulative and the artifact carries spend.usd_round.
spend_usd._also_not_instrumented: Stages 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 have no cost record for any certification.
